title: console-observability-triage-scratchpad-priya-2026-03-20
content:
Quick triage scratchpad for today (stream-of-consciousness)

Context:
- Customer-reported slow dashboard load for customer acme-inc during spike on 2026-03-19 (reported in RED-4321).
- Symptoms: dashboard tiles time out (spinner) after ~10s, page sometimes returns partial data (missing rps and errors charts).
- Affects: hosted console, predominantly us-west regions. Intermittent, correlated with backend slowness on metrics-aggregation service.

Immediate hypotheses / things to check:
- [ ] Aggregation job backlog on metrics-aggregation-prod (check queue depth, consumer lag).
- [ ] Redis connection pool exhaustion (look at maxclients, connection rates).
- [ ] Recent deploys: observability/metrics-aggregator v1.12.3 rolled 2026-03-18 ~22:30 UTC — could be related.
- [ ] Query timeouts from TSDB (prometheus long_query_threshold at 15s?) — customer queries may be heavier.
- [ ] Frontend change: dashboard batching change (PR #214) — confirm rollout percentage and fallback behavior.

Notes from quick logs/queries run so far:
- Ran: kubectl logs metrics-aggregator-*/ -n observability -> saw repeated WARN about partial shard reads starting ~2026-03-19T21:10Z.
- Grafana datasource errors: 502 gateway from metrics-aggregator at 21:12Z, spike of 120 errors in 5m window.
- Prometheus: several scrape targets showed increased scrape_duration_seconds 90th percentile from 200ms -> 1.8s around that time.
- Redis used_connections near maxclients for a few pods (metrics-agg-worker-2) between 21:05-21:20Z.

Immediate next actions (owner initials) — noise-prioritized:
- Priya: open temporary incident note in RED-4321 with timeline + affected customers (do now).
- Noah: check consumer lag for kinesis/metrics-raw-topic and forwarder errors (ask SRE to increase retention if needed).
- Maya: validate if prometheus queries for customer-specific dashboards have new heavy label filters (could be exploded cardinality).
- Eden: review PR #214 rollout % + canary logs; if 100% -> prepare rollback plan (prefill revert PR).

Short-term mitigations to try (if we see repeat outages):
- Increase metrics-aggregator replicas by +2 for autoscale buffer (short window, monitor cost).
- Temporarily increase Redis maxclients and restart affected pods gracefully (coord with infra).
- Enable fallback cache TTL for dashboard tiles longer (serve slightly stale data instead of spinner).

Questions / unknowns to follow up on:
- Is this only impacting dashboards with long time ranges (>24h) or all dashboards? (customer says both; need query logs).
- Are there any scheduled retention compaction jobs that ran around 21:00Z? (check infra maintenance calendar).
- Any recent config change to gateway/load-balancer healthchecks? Could cause 502s.

Customer comms TODOs:
- Draft note to ACME support contact (Sam Lee) acknowledging receipt and saying "we're investigating, will follow up in 2 hours" — Priya to send after initial triage.
- If mitigations applied, send follow-up with what we changed + ask for verification.

Longer-term follow-ups (add to backlog if recurring):
- Improve dashboard-level circuit breaker: if backend latency > X, show stale cached tile and surface warning.
- Add SLO for dashboard availability (percent of successful tile loads under 2s).
- Add more granular telemetry: tag requests by customer_id to quickly filter heavy queries.
- Performance runbook that covers Redis pooling, aggregator scaling, and query shaping.

Random notes / scratch items:
- We should ask product whether showing "partial data" is acceptable UX for now (flag in UI).
- Think about per-tenant query quotas or sampling for very large customers.
- Reuse existing cache layer (edge-cache) to serve top-level metrics more aggressively.

Log of quick timeline entries (for incident note):
- 2026-03-19T21:03Z - slack: acme-reports dashboard slow (ticket opened RED-4321).
- 2026-03-19T21:10Z - observed metrics-aggregator WARN partial shard reads.
- 2026-03-19T21:12Z - Grafana datasource 502 spike.
- 2026-03-20T09:30Z - initial triage (this doc).

Links to runbook / queries to paste in ticket:
- Kinesis consumer lag: aws cloudwatch query link (paste when I have browser).
- Redis slowlog & CONFIG GET maxclients (kubectl exec + redis-cli).
- Prometheus slow queries (UI -> status -> runtime & queries).

Notes to self for tomorrow:
- Re-run the aggregation job locally against subset of ACME data to reproduce latency.
- Schedule 30m with infra to discuss Redis pool sizing and connection tracking.
- Add an automated alert: if dashboard tile 95th p99 > 5s for >5m then page on-call SRE.

End of scratchpad. Will tidy and push key entries into RED-4321 incident note after pulling consumer lag metrics.

-- Priya
